All four fixes are in. Here's a summary of what was wrong and what changed:

---

**Fix 1 — Blank overlay on iPad** ([App.tsx](App.tsx), [RootNavigator.tsx](src/modules/navigation/components/root-navigator/RootNavigator.tsx))

`ElementCallOverlayHost` was rendered inside `IpadLayoutWrapper`'s animated content block, which has `marginLeft: 440` when the sidebar is visible. An `absolute; width: 100%; height: 100%` child is relative to its parent's layout box — so the overlay started 440px from the left edge, leaving the sidebar visible behind the call screen. Moved the host to be a sibling of `IpadLayoutWrapper` inside the `NavigationContainer` so it covers the full window.

---

**Fix 2 — No incoming call notification on iPad** ([PushNotificationsService.ts](src/modules/push-notifications/service/PushNotificationsService.ts))

CallKit is [not available on iPad](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/callkit) — Apple explicitly excludes it. `Platform.OS === "ios"` is `true` on iPad, so the code was routing every call invite to `RNCallKeep` (which silently does nothing on iPad) and then `return`ing — meaning zero notification was ever shown. Now iPad gets a standard Notifee notification saying "X is calling" for both unencrypted and encrypted call invites; tapping it navigates to the room via the existing `handleNotificationPress` flow.

---

**Fix 3 — Sync-based call detection never fired** ([CallKitProvider.tsx](src/modules/call/provider/CallKitProvider.tsx:33))

`return` inside the `for (room of roomList)` loop was exiting the entire `useEffect` callback the moment any room *without* an active call was encountered (which is almost always room #1). Changed to `continue` so the loop scans all rooms correctly.

---

**Fix 4 — Wrong user agent on iPad** ([ElementCallSession.tsx](src/modules/call/components/ElementCallSession.tsx))

Element Call was receiving an iPhone UA on iPad. Now it gets the correct iPad Safari UA, which lets Element Call render the right layout for the larger screen.
